subject: language
intro: I'm Mr. Brooks. Let's plan a lesson on how a poem's form contributes to its meaning.

beats.narration: The title connects form and meaning right away.
This standard asks students to analyze how a poem's form or structure contributes to its meaning.
Three specific structural features keep the analysis focused.
beats.text: Students will be able to analyze how line breaks, stanzas, and repetition contribute to a poem's meaning.

beats.narration: The side-by-side comparison makes structure visible.
beats.text: Show the same short poem written as a paragraph and as a poem. "Which one has more impact? Why?"

beats.narration: Thinking aloud about the poet's choices models analytical thinking.
beats.text: Model annotating a poem for line breaks (where the pauses fall), stanzas (shifts in idea), and repetition (emphasis). Think aloud about why the poet made each choice.

beats.narration: Rebuilding the poem forces them to think about structure.
beats.text: Groups get a poem cut into strips and try to arrange it. Then they compare with the original and discuss the poet's structural choices.

beats.narration: This keeps the focus on analysis.
beats.text: Choose one structural choice in today's poem and explain how it affects the meaning.

outro: Compare, model, rebuild, analyze. Now plan yours.
